The same split can occur from the vault side: [`StrategyVault.setProTokenPlus()`](https://github.com/promis-finance/promis-contracts/blob/4cd2d43122bf10c173b16d9a017415f35839c003/contracts/vaults/ProTokenPlus/StrategyVault.sol#L429-L437) allows independent rebinding of the vault's frontend reference with no migration or quiescence check.

#### Impact

Low. Changing the active vault pointer while live ProTokenPlus obligations exist can freeze pre-rotation user withdrawals. A legitimate unbonding that matured before rotation will revert when the user calls `completeWithdraw()` because the call is routed to the new vault, which holds no reserve for that cohort. The old vault retains the user's backing and funded withdrawal reserve but is no longer reachable through the live protocol entrypoints. New deposits after rotation flow into the replacement vault, splitting a single product's liabilities across multiple unrelated custody backends.

The old vault loses access to strategist settlement operations because `ProTokenOperations` authorization follows the live settings pointer. Without a built-in migration flow, governance must either roll the pointer back (potentially stranding users who interacted with the new vault in the meantime) or construct a bespoke recovery procedure. This leaves no safe on-chain recovery path and can strand user funds across vaults until manual intervention restores the correct linkage.

#### Recommendation

Prevent live vault rebinding unless an explicit migration flow is active. At minimum, make `setStrategyVault()` revert while ProTokenPlus has active positions, pending deposits, or active unbondings. If vault rotation must be supported, pause user actions, migrate or drain old-vault assets and ledgers in a single transaction, then update the pointer. Apply the same guard to `StrategyVault.setProTokenPlus()` to close the analogous unverified path. Consider binding each position and unbonding request to the vault address that holds its backing at creation time, so that completion operations can resolve the correct custodian regardless of subsequent pointer changes.

#### Developer Response

Acknowledged. `StrategyVault` rotation is very highly unlikely to happen once protocol is set. Additionally it will be documented.

issues.title: The module pause controls are disconnected from each other and `StrategyVault` has no pause mechanism of its own
issues.body:
#### Technical Details

Core and yield modules implement their circuit breaker by reading `ProTokenSettings.isPaused()`. For example, [`ProTokenOperations.whenNotPaused`](https://github.com/promis-finance/promis-contracts/blob/4cd2d43122bf10c173b16d9a017415f35839c003/contracts/core/ProTokenOperations.sol#L88-L93) uses the central setting.

The vault subsystem diverges in two ways:

- `ProTokenPlus` is pausable, but only locally: it inherits its own [`PausableUpgradeable`](https://github.com/promis-finance/promis-contracts/blob/4cd2d43122bf10c173b16d9a017415f35839c003/contracts/vaults/ProTokenPlus/ProTokenPlus.sol#L34) state.
- `StrategyVault` has no pause mechanism of its own: it neither inherits a pausable implementation nor checks `ProTokenSettings.isPaused()`. Its functions are stopped only where the call path happens to be gated elsewhere: [`borrow()`](https://github.com/promis-finance/promis-contracts/blob/4cd2d43122bf10c173b16d9a017415f35839c003/contracts/vaults/ProTokenPlus/StrategyVault.sol#L276)/[`repay()`](https://github.com/promis-finance/promis-contracts/blob/4cd2d43122bf10c173b16d9a017415f35839c003/contracts/vaults/ProTokenPlus/StrategyVault.sol#L321) transit through [`strategicUnmint()`](https://github.com/promis-finance/promis-contracts/blob/4cd2d43122bf10c173b16d9a017415f35839c003/contracts/core/ProTokenOperations.sol#L512-L516)/[`strategicMint()`](https://github.com/promis-finance/promis-contracts/blob/4cd2d43122bf10c173b16d9a017415f35839c003/contracts/core/ProTokenOperations.sol#L476-L479), which check the central pause, and the `onlyProTokenPlus` functions are covered by the local ProTokenPlus pause. The directly callable admin/operator functions [`rotate()`, `claimGrowth()`, and `claimYield()`](https://github.com/promis-finance/promis-contracts/blob/4cd2d43122bf10c173b16d9a017415f35839c003/contracts/vaults/ProTokenPlus/StrategyVault.sol#L356-L426) have no pause gate of any kind.

#### Impact

Low. Incident response is fragmented across two disconnected pause controls, and StrategyVault's direct operator functions answer to neither: with both `ProTokenSettings` and `ProTokenPlus` paused, `rotate()`, `claimGrowth()`, and `claimYield()` remain callable. In particular [`claimGrowth()`](https://github.com/promis-finance/promis-contracts/blob/4cd2d43122bf10c173b16d9a017415f35839c003/contracts/vaults/ProTokenPlus/StrategyVault.sol#L382-L402) transfers proUSD to an arbitrary recipient, so containment of a compromised operator key relies solely on rotating the role via [`ProTokenSettings.setOperator()`](https://github.com/promis-finance/promis-contracts/blob/4cd2d43122bf10c173b16d9a017415f35839c003/contracts/core/ProTokenSettings.sol#L73).

#### Recommendation

Consult one canonical circuit breaker, the central `ProTokenSettings.isPaused()`, from both `ProTokenPlus` and StrategyVault's directly callable privileged functions.

#### Developer Response

Acknowledged. It is intended.

issues.title: The unmint fee is unbounded
issues.body:
#### Technical Details

[`ProTokenSettings.setYAsset()`](https://github.com/promis-finance/promis-contracts/blob/4cd2d43122bf10c173b16d9a017415f35839c003/contracts/core/ProTokenSettings.sol#L151-L196) stores `unmintFeePer` without any bound. The field is documented in wad precision, where `1e18` represents 100%.

The fee is applied in [`ProTokenOperations._executeUnmint()`](https://github.com/promis-finance/promis-contracts/blob/4cd2d43122bf10c173b16d9a017415f35839c003/contracts/core/ProTokenOperations.sol#L390-L401):

```solidity
uint256 feeAmount = (yAssetToReceiveAmount *
    yAssetSettings.settings.unmintFeePer) / USD_PRECISION;
yAssetToReceiveAmount -= feeAmount;
```

In addition, `_executeUnmint()` runs during [`finalizeUnmintRequest()`](https://github.com/promis-finance/promis-contracts/blob/4cd2d43122bf10c173b16d9a017415f35839c003/contracts/core/ProTokenOperations.sol#L301-L343) and reads the yAsset settings fresh, so the fee charged is the one configured at finalization time, not the one in effect when the user created the request. A fee update therefore applies retroactively to every pending request, and the request's `minAmountOut` — fixed at creation and covered by the authority proof — is the user's only protection.

#### Impact

Low. A single unvalidated parameter can silently turn redemptions into near-total value capture for requests without slippage protection, or disable all approved unmints into the affected yAsset. Retroactive application to already-pending requests aggravates the issue. An explicit on-chain fee bound also removes this lever from the trust assumptions a proUSD holder must accept.

#### Recommendation

Introduce a `MAX_UNMINT_FEE` constant at a defensible business bound (e.g. `1e17` = 10%).

#### Developer Response

Fixed in commit [bb00e84](https://github.com/promis-finance/promis-contracts/commit/bb00e84a753e0955a56fd25d35e923dd373c9511):
- Unmint fee has now bound of 10%

issues.title: Median-relative validation permits oracle spreads above the configured maximum
issues.body:
#### Technical Details

`OracleAggregationSettings.maxPriceDeviation` is documented as the maximum allowed deviation [between oracle prices](https://github.com/promis-finance/promis-contracts/blob/4cd2d43122bf10c173b16d9a017415f35839c003/contracts/core/types/ProTokenOperationsTypes.sol#L26-L32). However, [`_validatePriceDeviation()`](https://github.com/promis-finance/promis-contracts/blob/4cd2d43122bf10c173b16d9a017415f35839c003/contracts/core/ProTokenOperations.sol#L955-L987) does not compare the sources to one another. It compares every source to the aggregated median.

For an even number of sources, [`_calculateMedianPrice()`](https://github.com/promis-finance/promis-contracts/blob/4cd2d43122bf10c173b16d9a017415f35839c003/contracts/core/ProTokenOperations.sol#L932-L953) defines the median as the arithmetic mean of the two central values. With exactly two prices `L` and `H`, this gives:

```text
M = (L + H) / 2
deviation(L, M) = deviation(H, M) = (H - L) / (H + L)
```

Therefore, a configured threshold `T` accepts any pair satisfying:

```text
H / L <= (1 + T) / (1 - T)
```

At the deployed 10% threshold, the two sources can have a price ratio of approximately `1.2222`. This is materially wider than the documented 10% maximum between the oracle responses. With only two sources, one faulty source can also move the returned arithmetic mean while neither response fails validation.

This can be monetized through [`_calculateUnmintAmount()`](https://github.com/promis-finance/promis-contracts/blob/4cd2d43122bf10c173b16d9a017415f35839c003/contracts/core/ProTokenOperations.sol#L728-L796), where an underestimated yAsset price is used as the redemption denominator.

#### Impact

Medium. A response pair whose direct spread exceeds the configured limit can still pass validation and produce a biased aggregate price. For redeemable assets, an underestimated aggregate price increases the number of yAsset units paid per burned proUSD, allowing repeated extraction from immediate reserves or creation of oversized queued liabilities.

Example scenario:

```text
oracle A:             1.00 USD
oracle B:             0.82 USD
maxPriceDeviation:    1000 BPS (10%)
calculated median:    0.91 USD
```

Both deviations from the median round to at most 10%, so [`_aggregateOraclePrices()`](https://github.com/promis-finance/promis-contracts/blob/4cd2d43122bf10c173b16d9a017415f35839c003/contracts/core/ProTokenOperations.sol#L896-L930) succeeds even though the sources differ far more than 10% relative to the `$1` response.

For a yAsset with a `$1` `usdCap`, a `$1` proUSD price, and no unmint fee, redeeming 100 proUSD uses the `$0.91` aggregate as the denominator and returns approximately 110 yAsset units. If the `$1` source is correct, the redeemer extracts about `$10` of excess collateral.

#### Recommendation

Validate a directly defined spread between `minPrice` and `maxPrice` in addition to, or instead of, per-source deviation from the median.

#### Developer Response

Fixed in commit [c5f6fae](https://github.com/promis-finance/promis-contracts/commit/c5f6fae727a1877d4a11650d13f471cfa9cf1407):
- Deviation check now includes spread

issues.title: Duplicate yield handlers double-count liquidity and can block redemptions
issues.body:
#### Technical Details

[`YAssetOperationsHandler.setYProtocolHandlers()`](https://github.com/promis-finance/promis-contracts/blob/4cd2d43122bf10c173b16d9a017415f35839c003/contracts/core/YAssetOperationsHandler.sol#L297-L339) validates array lengths, nonzero addresses, and total allocation, but it does not require handler addresses to be unique. A configuration such as `[H, H]` is therefore accepted.

Deposits through [`_allocateToHandlers()`](https://github.com/promis-finance/promis-contracts/blob/4cd2d43122bf10c173b16d9a017415f35839c003/contracts/core/YAssetOperationsHandler.sol#L420-L444) remain conserved: the allocation portions are deposited into the same handler in two calls, so handler `H` ultimately holds only the actual total deposited amount. However, [`previewPayOut()`](https://github.com/promis-finance/promis-contracts/blob/4cd2d43122bf10c173b16d9a017415f35839c003/contracts/core/YAssetOperationsHandler.sol#L347-L365) iterates over both entries and adds `H.getBalance()` twice. [`getYAssetInfo()`](https://github.com/promis-finance/promis-contracts/blob/4cd2d43122bf10c173b16d9a017415f35839c003/contracts/core/YAssetOperationsHandler.sol#L368-L385) has the same double-counting problem.

This creates a deterministic false positive in the ProTokenOperations instant-liquidity branch. If `previewPayOut()` returns true from the duplicated balance, [`payOut()`](https://github.com/promis-finance/promis-contracts/blob/4cd2d43122bf10c173b16d9a017415f35839c003/contracts/core/YAssetOperationsHandler.sol#L215-L262) withdraws the real balance from the first occurrence. The second occurrence then has no remaining balance, and `payOut()` ultimately reverts with `InsufficientBalance`. [`_executeUnmint()`](https://github.com/promis-finance/promis-contracts/blob/4cd2d43122bf10c173b16d9a017415f35839c003/contracts/core/ProTokenOperations.sol#L409-L434) propagates the revert instead of entering the asynchronous queue.

#### Impact

Low. Once configured, reported backing and previewed liquidity are inflated without any corresponding assets. Unmint and strategic-unmint transactions for amounts between the real and double-counted balance repeatedly revert instead of falling back to the queue. Any offchain NAV or monitoring process consuming `getYAssetInfo()` can also overstate protocol backing.

#### Recommendation

Reject duplicate handler addresses in `setYProtocolHandlers()`. The function already clears every old handler's `isProtocolHandler` flag before inserting the new set, so at insertion time the flag is `true` only if the same address appeared earlier in the new array. Checking it before writing is sufficient:

```diff
  for (uint256 i = 0; i < handlersLength; i++) {
      address handlerAddr = _handlers[i];
      uint256 allocation = _allocations[i];

+     if (isProtocolHandler[handlerAddr]) revert DuplicateHandler();
      isProtocolHandler[handlerAddr] = true;
```

#### Developer Response

Fixed in commit [05c72e1](https://github.com/promis-finance/promis-contracts/commit/05c72e1bef3c3948c091e93bb51badfb90fde582):
- Added duplicate check
